scenes.title: 모델은 같은데 자세가 달라진다
lines: Watch Tekken’s Lili extend one leg into a kick. Even with the same character, turning the head, shoulders and feet changes the impression. One foot rises high, but the planted foot still tells us where the force goes. Let's adjust a pose and examine the line of the body, the outline of the hands and arms, and how the feet carry weight. An articulated figure is a good way to study these relationships. Bend an arm, turn the torso and change your viewing angle to see which shapes are easier to read. In realistic and exaggerated poses alike, you can see where someone is looking and which foot bears their weight.

scenes.title: 먼저 전후 차이를 본다
lines: Let's compare a straight stance with the adjusted pose. The model, clothing and light are identical. Only the arrangement of the body changes. In the final pose the head and torso face different directions, and the arms and feet play distinct roles. When the fighters face off, the face watches the opponent while the forward hand guards the space between them. You needn't learn all the changes at once. Let's go back and adjust one part at a time. If several things move together, it's easy to miss which one changed the impression.

scenes.title: 머리에서 다리로 이어지는 흐름
lines: First, let's break the left-right symmetry. Turn the torso a little away from the camera and lower the chin. Tilt the head toward a point of interest. Now we see where the face looks and where the body braces. As Lili lifts the teacup, her chin tilts toward it and the hand leaves her face clear. Next, look at the torso, pelvis and legs. A rigid straight line through them can make the pose stiff. Give them slightly different directions to create a flow through the body. A gently bending line like this is often called an S-curve. Start by deciding where the character is looking and how they're standing. Then trace a line over the pose to see if that relationship reads.

scenes.title: 옷과 어깨도 같은 방향을 말한다
lines: With the body in place, look at the clothes and props. Angle the scarf so its direction reinforces the turn of the body. Fanning the cloth a little can carry the line of the pose. Back in the fight, watch the hem fan out as the torso turns. It reinforces the direction of the rotation. The skirt or clothes on a physical figure may be fixed in one shape. Separate what the figure allows from how you'd like cloth to flow on the character. Open the shoulders and lift them slightly if the arms need that support.

scenes.title: 팔과 손을 따로 읽히게
lines: Let's give the arms different angles. Bend each arm enough to read against the torso while keeping it close to the body. Remove colors and patterns and check whether the outline still tells you where the arm points. That outer shape is the silhouette. Donkey Kong’s hand stands out against his torso. Its silhouette reveals the swing before we read the face. Now adjust the wrist. A straight line from forearm to fingertips can look like a stick. A slight bend distinguishes an active hand from a relaxed one. Carry the intent of the pose all the way to the fingertips.

scenes.title: 어디에 무게를 싣고 있는가
lines: Now look for the leg that takes the weight. Start with weight divided equally and shift some onto one leg. The torso and pelvis respond, changing the character's attitude. The hunter lowers the torso and puts one foot forward after the swing. Footing changes how the body supports the weapon. Turn the toes slightly outward and put one foot a little closer to the camera. The floor grid makes it easy to see which foot is forward. Our guide line helps you read the stance. It doesn't measure the actual center of mass. For parts that spread outward, like wings, check that they appear to have depth. Angle them so you can see what projects forward and what recedes. The attachments and the body should occupy the same space.

scenes.title: 부분을 합친 뒤 다시 판단한다
lines: After those small adjustments, look at the entire pose again. The head, shoulders, hands and feet must still work together. These techniques are ways of judging the result. What matters is the impression the whole pose gives. A running or attacking pose also needs to suggest the direction and force of the movement. Even a detailed character illustration depends on a strong underlying pose. Even in a small picture, Lili’s extended leg reads apart from her opponent. That information survives the loss of detail. Mentally remove the decoration and see if the action and personality still read.

scenes.title: 자세를 보는 눈을 연습하기
lines: Posing a figure and turning it helps you see how the parts relate. You can repeat this comparison with an articulated character. Let's put our final pose beside the starting pose. With the same body, the action and the character's attitude are clearer.
